messages:
maya: Ran a 2h perf run on large-13B, microbatch=8. Observed p99 jump from ~120ms -> ~320ms when kv_miss_rate > 20%. logs below.
perfbot: alert: p99_regression detected (run=2026-03-10T14:22Z) trace=trace-abc123 :rotating_light:
alex: Noticed similar on Friday. Seems kernel A (fast-attn) is great on warm KV but regresses on cold KV because of cache miss tail and different kernel latency curve.
sam: Numbers? can you paste a small table?
maya: 
```
mb=8  | throughput=4800 tok/s | p95=110ms | p99=320ms | kv_miss=0.22
mb=4  | throughput=3600 tok/s | p95=95ms  | p99=150ms | kv_miss=0.22
mb=8 + prefetch | throughput=4300 | p99=180ms | kv_miss=0.05
```
kai: Hm. microbatch 8 saturates GPU but amplifies tail when KV misses. Options: lower mb, change kernel selection, or improve prefetch/warmup.
alex: Propose heuristic: prefer kernel B (stable tail) if recent_kv_miss_rate > 0.15 OR observed_tail_prob > 0.05 for sequences > 512. Keep kernel A otherwise.
sam: We also need admission control change: soft-admit that keeps headroom target at 65% instead of 80% during KV-missy workloads. That reduces throughput but stabilizes p99.
maya: Draft config for canary:
```
kernel_selection:
  fallback_threshold_kv_miss: 0.18
  seq_len_cutoff: 512
  tail_prob_cutoff: 0.05
admission:
  mode: soft
  headroom_target: 0.65
  drop_priority: low
prefetch:
  kv_prefetch_enabled: true
  kv_warmup_window_sec: 30
```
alex: run canary on 2 GPUs for 2h, 10% traffic. measure p95/p99, throughput, and cost delta.
perfbot: canary job queued: job=canary-2123456789 model=large-13B traffic=10% window=2h :white_check_mark:
maya: ok i'll schedule for 14:00 UTC today. watch metrics in console /dashboards/eng-runtime/canaries
sam: If this stabilizes p99 we can tune headroom back up or add adaptive scaling that increases batch size when kv_miss drops.
kai: Let's also add a tiny probe that forces a kernel switch if single-request latency exceeds 500ms.
maya: agreed. i'll post canary results in this thread. :rocket:
